topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, learning outcomes, and conceptual overview for studying the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulated Growth Signaling and Pathway Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in pathways such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases drive growth factor independence and sustained proliferation.

topics.label: Block to Terminal Differentiation in Hematopoietic and Epithelial Tissues
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how oncogenic alterations prevent cells from exiting the cell cycle into fully differentiated functional states in leukemia and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere Dynamics, Replicative Immortality, and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms of telomere shortening, senescence induction, cancer-specific telomerase reactivation, and p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Cancer Metabolic Rewiring and Oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics transition to complex cancer hallmarks and explain aerobic glycolysis, tissue metabolic differences, and Krebs cycle mutations producing oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and Vascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how tumors overcome hypoxia and nutrient limits by activating the angiogenic switch to form new blood vessels.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Inefficiency, and Genomics of Tumor Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cells for monitoring, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and genomic characteristics of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Summary and Concluding Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of the hallmarks and closing administrative remarks.
